newsitem.title: USA: U.S. automakers say strong dlr hurting Japan sales.
newsitem.headline: U.S. automakers say strong dlr hurting Japan sales.

text.p: The American Automobile Manufacturers Association on Friday repeated concerns that the strong dollar and weak yen are hurting efforts to boost automotive exports to Japan.
"The weak yen, now in the 120-123 yen per dollar range, continues to undercut the three companies' efforts to reach Japanese consumers," the association said in a press release.

The association, representing the Big Three Automakers -- Ford, Chrysler and General Motors -- noted that a recent report by the American Chamber of Commerce in Japan that said the weak yen "poses the greatest threat to progress on the bilateral trade imbalance and improved access for foreign vehicles and parts in Japan."
The trade association complained that a 1995 trade agreement aimed at boosting U.S. auto and parts sales in Japan was not living up to expectations.

"With each month, Japan's government and auto industry fall further behind in meeting the modest expectations outlined at the time of the trade pacts signing," AAMA President Andrew Card said in a statement.

"We expected meaningful deregulation and a sincere effort to encourage Japanese dealers to sell imported cars and trucks," he said. "What we've gotten is a lot of lip service and little to back it up."
